before.title: Dual-Clutch Transmission (DCT) Shudder at Low Speeds
before.description: The 7-speed dual-clutch transmission (7G-DCT) in the B-Class develops a noticeable shudder during low-speed maneuvers and from a standstill. The issue stems from clutch pack wear and adaptive software that struggles to compensate as the clutch material thins over time.
before.solution: Start with a DCT adaptation reset via Mercedes XENTRY diagnostic tool. If shudder persists, the dual-clutch assembly requires replacement. Updated clutch packs with revised friction material are available and significantly improve longevity.

citations.title: MBWorld.org — B-Class DCT shudder and clutch replacement discussion thread

communityRecommendations.content: A transmission adaptation reset often buys time, but the clutch pack will eventually need replacement. Budget for it around 60,000-80,000 miles.

before.title: Electric Drive Motor Whine and Bearing Noise (B250e)
before.description: The B250e electric drive unit produces an abnormal high-pitched whine or growling noise that increases with speed. The noise originates from worn bearings in the electric motor or the single-speed reduction gear. Tesla supplied the drivetrain components, and parts availability has become limited.
before.solution: Diagnose whether the noise is from the motor bearings or reduction gear. Motor bearing replacement is possible at specialized EV shops. If the reduction gear is worn, the entire drive unit may need replacement. Check with Mercedes for remaining parts availability as the B250e is discontinued.
symptoms: High-pitched whine that increases with speed
Noise changes character with regenerative braking

citations.title: MBWorld.org — B250e electric drive motor noise diagnosis and parts sourcing

communityRecommendations.content: Parts for the B250e are becoming scarce since the Tesla-sourced drivetrain is discontinued. Address noise early before bearing damage becomes catastrophic and destroys the motor.

proposal.title: Electric Drive Motor Whine and Bearing Noise (B250e)

before.title: Turbocharger Oil Feed Line Leak
before.description: The turbo oil feed line on the M270 engine in the B-Class develops leaks at the banjo bolt connection on top of the turbocharger. Oil drips onto the hot exhaust manifold, producing a burning oil smell and visible smoke from the engine bay.
before.solution: Replace the turbo oil feed line and both copper crush washers at the banjo bolt connections. Inspect the turbo for bearing play while the line is disconnected. Clean oil residue from the exhaust manifold to eliminate the burning smell.

before.title: Electronic Parking Brake Actuator Malfunction
before.description: W246 owners report the electronic parking brake (EPB) sticking or showing a malfunction warning on the dashboard. The fault is typically a failing parking-brake actuator motor, corroded cables/connectors, or a software glitch in the control module. The brake may fail to release, refuse to apply, or trigger an EPB warning, which can immobilize the car or require service before driving.
before.solution: Fault-read the EPB control module with XENTRY/STAR. Inspect and clean cabling and connectors, update/recalibrate the EPB control-module software if a glitch is found, and replace the parking-brake actuator motor if it has failed. Recalibrate the system after any actuator or cable replacement.

before.title: M270 Timing Chain Stretch and Cold-Start Rattle (Petrol)
before.description: The turbo petrol M270 (and naturally-aspirated M270/M274 in B180/B200/B250) uses a two-stage timing chain whose plastic guide rails and hydraulic tensioner degrade prematurely. Owners report a loud metallic rattle for roughly 1-15 seconds on cold start that fades as oil pressure builds. Short-trip urban use accelerates the problem because the cold-start period (low oil pressure) makes up a large share of running time. Stretch typically appears from ~80,000 km (50,000 mi), with some city cars rattling from ~70,000 km. Left unaddressed, chain stretch alters valve timing, throws fault codes, and risks contact/wear on cam bearings and phasers.
before.solution: Diagnose with a cold-start listen and read live chain/cam-position data via XENTRY. If only the tensioner is at fault, replacing the hydraulic chain tensioner first is the cheaper initial fix; if the chain is stretched, replace the complete OEM timing kit (chain, both guide rails, tensioner, and cam phaser sprockets if worn) to avoid consequential damage. Use the correct MB-Approval 229.5/229.51 0W-40 or 5W-40 oil and shorten oil-change intervals on short-trip cars.
symptoms: Metallic rattle on cold start lasting 1-15 seconds

before.title: OM651 Diesel DPF and EGR Clogging (B180 CDI / B200 CDI)
before.description: The 2.2L OM651 diesel in B180 CDI / B200 CDI variants is prone to diesel particulate filter (DPF) blockage and EGR-valve carbon fouling, especially on short urban trips where the exhaust never reaches regeneration temperature. Symptoms include reduced power (limp mode), increased fuel consumption, frequent failed regenerations, and warning lights. Carbon buildup in the EGR valve and intake also causes hesitation and rough running. The OM651 timing chain can also stretch and rattle, compounding diesel reliability concerns.
before.solution: Take the car for sustained high-speed driving to allow a complete regeneration; if the DPF is heavily loaded, perform a forced regen via XENTRY or a professional DPF clean, and in severe cases replace the DPF. Clean or replace a fouled EGR valve and clear intake carbon. Read soot-load and differential-pressure data to confirm. Diagnose and fix any underlying cause (failed glow plugs, leaking injectors, faulty differential-pressure sensor) before replacing the filter. Maintain with correct low-SAPS oil and longer drive cycles.

before.title: Panoramic Sunroof Drain Clog and Water Leak
before.description: W246 cars fitted with the panoramic glass roof suffer water ingress when the front-corner sunroof drain tubes clog with leaves and debris, or when the perimeter rubber seal wears. Owners report water entering at the front edge / A-pillar area and pooling in the footwell, with damp carpet, headliner staining, and musty smells. The drains are located at the right and left front of the sunroof. Trapped water can also reach electrical modules under the carpet.
before.solution: Inspect and flush the four sunroof drain tubes with low-pressure compressed air or a gentle water stream to clear debris; verify water exits at the rocker/sill outlets. Inspect and replace the perimeter sunroof seal if cracked, shrunken, or deformed. Dry the carpet/headliner and check underfloor connectors for corrosion. Periodic drain cleaning is the key preventive step.
symptoms: Dripping at A-pillar or front roof edge

before.title: Plastic Thermostat Housing Coolant Leak (M270)
before.description: The M270/M274 petrol engines use a map-controlled, electronically actuated thermostat integrated into a plastic housing that cracks or warps with age and heat cycling, becoming a common slow coolant-leak point. Early symptoms are a sweet coolant smell from the engine bay and a gradually dropping coolant level with no visible puddle (it evaporates on hot surfaces), plus temperature-gauge fluctuation or slow warm-up as the thermostat starts sticking. On a cold-day test drive the car should reach ~80 C within 10-15 minutes; if it hovers below, suspect the thermostat. It is an expensive, dealer-favored repair because of access.
before.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the thermostat housing for seepage. Replace the complete thermostat/housing assembly with the genuine Mercedes part (aftermarket replicas have a high repeat-failure rate on M270), refill with the correct MB-spec coolant, and bleed the system. Address any concurrent water-pump weep-hole leak at the same time.
symptoms: Sweet coolant smell from engine bay
Slowly dropping coolant with no visible puddle
Slow warm-up / engine not reaching ~80 C

before.title: Tailgate / Boot Lock Actuator Electrical Failure
before.description: The W246 tailgate (boot) locking system is a frequently reported electrical weak point. Corroded contacts in the lock actuator, a defective interior release lever, or water ingress from a leaking rear-washer hose cause the boot to fail to open or lock. Keyless-Go interaction and a weak key battery can compound the symptom. Electrical faults account for a large share of W246 complaints, and the tailgate lock is among the most-cited. The emergency release cable behind the rear seat backrest is the temporary workaround when the boot will not open.
before.solution: Clean the actuator contacts with electrical contact cleaner and apply dielectric grease (preventive cleaning roughly every 30,000 km is advised). Repair or re-solder corroded wiring (a Mercedes repair kit with heat-shrink is commonly used). For a permanently defective actuator, replace the lock actuator and re-teach the component via XENTRY. Fix any leaking rear-washer hose that allows water into the lock mechanism, and dry/clean affected connectors.
symptoms: Boot/tailgate will not open from button or key
Must use emergency release cable behind rear seat
